summary: @qlik/prettier-config preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a shared Prettier configuration but declares a `preinstall` lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (`_0x`-prefixed identifiers, inline lookup tables) and, when `bun` is absent from PATH, downloads a Bun runtime zip from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip`, extracts it, chmods 0755, and uses `execFileSync` to run the sibling file `math_init.js` under that freshly fetched runtime. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, rotating string/number array via a `WV8StW` shift routine, hex-mangled identifiers) with no accompanying source or documentation. setup.mjs additionally fingerprints the host with `execFileSync('ldd', ['--version'])` and reads `/etc/os-release` for Alpine/musl detection. A Prettier configuration package has no legitimate reason to fetch a language runtime, perform OS fingerprinting, or execute a large obfuscated payload at install time; the behavior is inconsistent with the declared purpose and matches an alternate-runtime-dropper pattern that runs attacker-controlled code on the installer's host during `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
